full_judgment: 5. Mr Azad cites an unreported decision pronounced in CR case No. 943 of 1989 on the same point by a Single Bench finding that the pre-emption cannot be allowed as there is no Khatian Number or Plot Number. The said decision is not binding upon this court. It has only persuasive force. After State Acquisition and Tenancy Act came in 1950 the owners and possessors of all kinds of lands have become direct tenants under the Government. The pre-emptor being a co-sharer and the purchaser, being stranger, case land being part of a holding that is portion of a compact land, although there is no Khatian Number or plot Number of the transferred land, it constitutes a part of an agriculture holding according to section 96(1) and section 2(13) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act. So, pre-emption, in the instant case, is to be allowed. The pre-emption case under section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act has been filed within 4 (four) months from the date of knowledge. Appellate Court has rightly and legally allowed pre-emption. There is no illegality in the judgment and order of the appellate Court resulting in an error in. the decision occasioning failure of justice.
